findings.title: Prometheus exposition injection and unbounded cardinality via the raw request path
findings.evidence: One unauthenticated GET to /x%22%7D%20999999%0Ahttp_requests_total%7B...%22500%22%7D%20424242%0A%23%20x (404) made GET /metrics emit the well-formed forged sample http_requests_total{method="GET",route="/health",status="500"} 424242, and swallowed the genuine 404 sample into a comment line. A separate probe produced a duplicate 'status' label, which makes the whole scrape unparseable. 150 distinct 404 paths produced 154 permanent series and a 13696-byte body.
findings.impact: Integrity loss on the channel that observability.slo.error_rate_pct is computed from (fabricate or mask a 5xx rate), plus unbounded process memory growth from unauthenticated 404 traffic. /metrics is public per api-contracts.md:38.

findings.title: decimal.Overflow escapes Money.multiply
findings.evidence: Money(2).multiply(Decimal('1E+999999999')) raises decimal.Overflow in 0.0 ms (not InvalidMoneyAmountError) because _quantize catches only InvalidOperation and the multiplication applies the context first. Money(2).multiply(10**999999) raises the right type but costs 9708.5 ms of CPU; 10**500000 costs 2430.5 ms. The constructor path is safe.
findings.impact: A raw decimal exception escapes a Types-layer value object, becoming a 500 instead of a 422; and a 9.7 s blocking computation on the event loop.
findings.correction: The prior finding's mechanism was partly wrong: the integer-scalar shape does NOT leak Overflow; only the Decimal-scalar shape does.

findings.title: Registered PII outlives its request scope as lru_cache keys
findings.evidence: _redaction_pattern is @lru_cache(maxsize=256) keyed by the sensitive value. After request 1 closed its scope: CacheInfo(hits=0, misses=2, currsize=2); request 2 registering the same PAN/Aadhaar gave hits=2 - a cache hit is only possible if request 1's PII was still stored as a key. An unrelated third request left currsize=3.
findings.impact: Up to 256 applicants' PAN/Aadhaar stay resident in process memory indefinitely (cache keys and compiled pattern objects), visible in a core dump. Contradicts the module docstring's 'Registration is request-scoped'.

findings.title: X-Request-ID accepted unvalidated and unbounded
findings.evidence: 200000-char id accepted -> 200, echoed in full in the response header, 200146-byte log line. 10000-char id -> 10146-byte line. 'a", "level": "CRITICAL", "x": "\' reflected verbatim into the response header and the request_id field. latin-1 bytes (0xff 0xfe) echoed raw in a response header. No length cap, charset check or format gate.
findings.impact: Attacker-controlled unbounded value written to every log line and echoed in a response header; hostile to any downstream pipeline that greps or re-serialises. Fails open.

findings.title: Money wire parser silently accepts non-wire-format strings
findings.evidence: Money('12_34') -> 1234.00 (silent 100x misread, Python Decimal accepts underscores); Money('  12.34  ') -> 12.34; Money('1e-999999') -> 0.00.
findings.impact: D-G specifies a quoted 2dp string; there is no format gate, so a malformed input is coerced rather than rejected.

findings.title: Redaction coverage is a one-shot enumeration at configure time
findings.evidence: Negative control: a logger created after configure_logging has no RedactionFilter (has_filter=False). It is still scrubbed in practice because it propagates to the root handler, which carries its own RedactionFilter.
findings.impact: Residual risk is a future library logger with propagate=False or its own handler - exactly what uvicorn does, and why _JSON_ROUTED_LOGGERS is a hardcoded three-name list.

findings.title: Money's magnitude ceiling and multiply rounding depend on the ambient decimal context
findings.evidence: With decimal.getcontext().prec = 6, Money('123456789.99') raises InvalidMoneyAmountError; at the default prec=28 it is fine. Money never opens a localcontext. Undocumented ceiling ~1e26: Money('1'+'0'*26) raises.
findings.impact: Third-party code lowering the thread-local precision silently changes the ceiling and intermediate rounding of a type whose purpose is that money never drifts. Fails closed (exception, not a wrong number).

findings.title: HEAD /health returns 405
findings.evidence: HEAD /health -> 405 {"error":"HTTPError","detail":"Method Not Allowed"}. FastAPI's @router.get does not register HEAD.
findings.impact: Load balancers and uptime monitors defaulting to HEAD read the service as unhealthy. Not an AC violation (AC5 and the contract specify GET); operational note for E15-S2.

findings.title: DPD classifier has no runtime type guard
findings.evidence: classify_by_days_past_due(29.9) -> CURRENT; (True) -> CURRENT; ('35') -> bare TypeError; classify(datetime, date) -> bare TypeError.
findings.impact: Signature says int and mypy covers first-party callers; negative cases raise TypeError rather than the module's own ValueError contract.

refuted_candidates.evidence: All raise InvalidMoneyAmountError; multiply(Decimal('NaN')) too; the wire path rejects 'NaN', 'Infinity', a JSON float and a JSON int.

refuted_candidates.candidate: SEC-008 as written - an integer scalar leaks decimal.Overflow
refuted_candidates.evidence: multiply(10**999999) raises InvalidMoneyAmountError. Only the Decimal-scalar shape leaks; recorded corrected as G3-F2.

refuted_candidates.candidate: SEC-009 - frontend money rendering hangs on a pathological exponent
refuted_candidates.evidence: decimal.js live: 1e10000 toFixed(2) = 1 ms, 1e100000 = 4 ms, 1e1000000 = 40 ms (linear in digits, no hang); 1e9000000000000000 stays finite; NaN rejected by isFinite. Downgrade to informational.
